title: The Matching Sand Shovels Incident
skyStory: A thread of a crescent, only six percent awake, floats in Pisces like a fish fin glimpsed under dark water. Pisces deals in echoes and doubles, and tonight it is feeling generous. Two things that should not match will match. Saturn is checking its notes twice. Mars is pretending not to have arranged anything. The fin flicks once.

reading: Today the universe runs a copy machine. Something you say before noon will be repeated, word for word, by a total stranger before supper. You will want to scream. Don't even scream. Just write it down with the time.

The Tiger usually pounces first and asks questions later, but the echo wants you still. When the repeat happens, take it as a nudge that the idea you have been circling is worth one real step this week. Not ten steps. One. Life Path 3 loves an audience, and today the cosmos is the audience, quietly repeating your lines back to you so you hear how good they sound.
joel.mission: Pick an unusual word at breakfast, something like marmalade or lighthouse, and count how many times it shows up today.
joel.omen: Two pigeons on a ledge turning their heads in perfect unison. You are in sync with something bigger, so trust today's hunch.

reading: You will find a child's plastic sand shovel poking out of a melting snowbank this morning, the kind of spring relic winter gives back. Remember its colour. By 4 pm you will see its exact twin somewhere else entirely.

This is the kind of thing only a Wood Rat notices, and that is the point. Your eye for the tiny detail is the whole trick of Life Path 11. When the second shovel appears, tell someone the story with both hands, and watch them not believe you. Then text Joel the colour. He will reply with something that matches, and you will both say the same three letters at once.
nancy.mission: Photograph any lost toy you spot today, a shovel, a ball, a tiny truck, and give it a hopeful name, like it is waiting for a reunion.
nancy.omen: A song playing in two different places within an hour. It means the echo has found you too.

together.text: DES day, officially. Each of you guess one random object the other will see today: a blue bucket, a cat in a window, a kite stuck in a tree. Swap guesses at noon, report back at dark. If either guess lands, ΔΕΣ is written in the sky.
